channel.title: Aristotle
channel.description: Aristotle's own words, read in full, with plain-spoken commentary that breaks each idea down to first principles.

item.title: Ethics III · 8 — Five Things That Look Like Courage
item.description: Social pressure, experience, rage, overconfidence, and ignorance can all look like bravery. Aristotle shows why only one motive makes courage real. Full chapter read, with commentary.
item.itunes:summary: Social pressure, experience, rage, overconfidence, and ignorance can all look like bravery. Aristotle shows why only one motive makes courage real. Full chapter read, with commentary.

item.title: Ethics III · 7 — The Brave, the Reckless, and the Coward
item.description: Courage is the middle between too much fear and too much boldness. Why the reckless person is often a coward in costume. Full chapter read, with commentary.
item.itunes:summary: Courage is the middle between too much fear and too much boldness. Why the reckless person is often a coward in costume. Full chapter read, with commentary.

item.title: Ethics III · 6 — What Courage Is About
item.description: Not every fearlessness is courage. Aristotle narrows courage down to facing the greatest danger for a noble reason. Full chapter read, with commentary.
item.itunes:summary: Not every fearlessness is courage. Aristotle narrows courage down to facing the greatest danger for a noble reason. Full chapter read, with commentary.

item.title: Ethics III · 5 — We Are Responsible for Our Character
item.description: Character is built by repeated actions, so it is ours. The thrown stone, the inner eye, and why you can't wish your way out of a habit. Full chapter read, with commentary.

item.title: Ethics III · 4 — What We Wish For
item.description: Do we wish for what is good, or for what only seems good? Aristotle's answer, the good person as a measuring stick, and why pleasure fools us. Full chapter read, with commentary.

item.title: Ethics III · 3 — Thinking Things Through
item.description: We only deliberate about what is up to us, and we think about the route, not the destination. Aristotle on how good planning actually works. Full chapter read, with commentary.

item.title: Ethics III · 2 — What Choice Is
item.description: Choice is not desire, anger, wishing, or belief. Aristotle narrows it down until only one thing is left. Full chapter read, with commentary.

item.title: Ethics III · 1 — Willing and Unwilling Actions
item.description: When is something truly your doing? Aristotle separates forced acts and honest mistakes from everything else, which is yours. Full chapter read, with commentary.
